title: Reality Gate: Held-Out Viability Veto
question: When continuous ranking is weak, can sequence-derived models still conservatively veto candidates likely to violate a joint developability viability region, thereby saving experiments while retaining experimentally clean antibodies?

prior_work_boundary.CPG-002: INCONCLUSIVE_COVERAGE; composite and hard-veto arms both had 0.0 declared gated-liability rate across four GDPa1 folds.
prior_work_boundary.trial_selector: Small external sample and wide uncertainty; does not establish a useful selector.
prior_work_boundary.new_mechanism_under_test: Continuous per-assay prediction with training-only one-sided residual bounds over a joint viability region. This is not another composite-vs-hard-threshold rerun.

test.name: GDPa3
test.role: untouched external holdout; no parameter selection on GDPa3 labels

excluded_primary.Titer: Excluded from primary endpoint because production-condition dependence makes it less suitable for the frozen viability claim.

robustness.description: Predeclared ±5% threshold stress test. This is a robustness probe, not a claim about published assay uncertainty.

dispositions.VETO: High-confidence predicted violation; do not spend the next experiment under this gate.
dispositions.UNKNOWN: No high-confidence veto; candidate remains eligible for experiment.
dispositions.PASS: Forbidden. Surviving the gate does not certify a good antibody.

kill_condition: If RGV cannot preserve >=95% of experimentally clean GDPa3 antibodies, avoid >=50% of experiments, and exceed the best nonrandom baseline by >=10 percentage points in experiment avoidance while preserving the same clean-retention floor, close the learned-veto hypothesis. Do not rescue it by changing thresholds or redefining cleanliness after seeing GDPa3.
